title: Define inbound compatibility-hints schema and acceptance rubric for open-model catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: remove ambiguity at intake by requiring a small, machine-validated "compatibility-hints" payload from contributors of open models. The payload should be minimal (to reduce friction) but sufficient for runtime routing, pin decisions, and automated fallback selection. This ticket defines the v1 hints schema, the acceptance rubric (automated and manual checks), and the on-ramp for models that cannot provide every hint. It also clarifies how the runtime should interpret missing or contradictory signals and what constitutes a soft-pin vs a hard pin. Key trade-offs considered: lowering friction for community submissions vs. operational safety for production routes, and the risk of false-positive compatibility assertions from model owners.

The document contains: required fields, optional fields, validation rules, semantic meaning of each hint, default runtime behaviors, acceptance criteria for catalog ingest, scope exclusions, rollout plan and QA tests.

Context: Multiple PMs and the runtime team observed recurring manual triage for community model submissions where lack of clear runtime signals caused deployment regressions or unexpected latency/cost spikes. The catalog team needs a lightweight contract that reduces manual reviews while keeping the door open for experimental variants.
background: Existing intake forms accept freeform text and a long-form README. Engineering currently does runtime heuristics based on binary tests that are brittle. Design and product want a machine-readable shim (compatibility-hints) that is opinionated but minimal. Prior tickets explored pinning semantics and soft-fallbacks but did not standardize a compact schema or acceptance rubric. This ticket unblocks automation for auto-tagging models into 'can-route-to-low-latency' vs 'batch-only' pools and will reduce manual review queue by expected 40%.
schema_v1_summary: Fields are simple key:value pairs; all keys are lowercase dash-separated
Required keys: model_family, variant_note, arch_signature, nominal_flops_gflops, preferred_runtime_profile
Optional but recommended: hf_repo_id, seq_length_tail, kv_cache_compatible (yes/no), quant_levels (comma-separated), known_failure_modes
Each numeric field must include units where appropriate (e.g., gflops) and may be a single number or a small range like '6-7'
Max payload size: 2KB; aim for <1KB in practice
semantic_definitions: model_family: canonical short name used in catalog (e.g., 'redwood-rl-v1' or 'llama2-70b')
arch_signature: string describing architecture family and tokenizer coupling (e.g., 'transformer-xl-std:tiktoken-v1')
nominal_flops_gflops: coarse compute footprint used for capacity planning and kernel-selection
preferred_runtime_profile: one of ['latency-sensitive', 'throughput-optimized', 'mixed'] used by routing policies
kv_cache_compatible: explicit yes/no indicating whether KV cache semantics match our runtime; 'unknown' allowed but triggers manual review
quant_levels: e.g., '8,4' or 'int4' to indicate supported quantizations
validation_rules: Reject if required keys missing (automated) unless proposer indicates 'experimental: true' in optional flags
nominal_flops_gflops must be parsable as positive number or range; otherwise flag for manual review
preferred_runtime_profile defaults to 'mixed' if absent; absence reduces auto-route confidence but does not block ingest
kv_cache_compatible set to 'yes' required for routing into low-latency cached pools; 'unknown' or 'no' means automatically mark as 'warm-only' until manual validation
hf_repo_id when present must resolve to a public repo within 48 hours or be marked 'private' with supporting provenance links
acceptance_criteria: Automated validation accepts >=90% of incoming community payloads without manual edits (after a brief doc update window)
If kv_cache_compatible='yes', runtime smoke test (end-to-end inference with 1k tokens) completes within catalog's latency SLO or ticket is created
If preferred_runtime_profile='latency-sensitive', an automated perf profile must be generated within 24h and attached to the catalog entry
Models marked 'experimental' may be ingested with partial hints but require 'experimental' label and are ineligible for auto-forwarding to Dedicated pools
Every accepted model has at least one provenance link (hf_repo_id, docker image, or signed artifact) in the catalog entry
scope_inclusions: Define v1 schema and automated validation rules
Runtime interpretation defaults for missing or conflicting hints
Small UX change to intake form to capture the compact hints schema
scope_exclusions: Automated in-depth perf/regression testing beyond smoke profiles
Full integration with enterprise Private onboarding flow in this ticket (follow-on)
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize schema and doc update (this ticket)
2) Add machine validator to intake API (ENG) - soft-launch behind a flag
3) Run vetting on last 500 community submissions to surface edge cases
4) Enable auto-accept for 'mixed' and 'throughput-optimized' with confidence thresholds
5) After 2 weeks, expand to kv_cache_compatible='yes' auto-route with runtime smoke test gating
qa_tests: Unit tests for schema validator covering missing/extra fields and malformed numeric ranges
End-to-end test: create a new catalog entry with sample compat payload and assert correct auto-tagging and smoke-test behavior
Regression checklist to ensure no existing pinned models are reclassified unexpectedly
Manual review playbook for 'unknown' kv_cache_compatible or inconsistent arch_signature
acceptance_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: model owners misreport kv_cache_compatible leading to latency regressions. Mitigation: require smoke-test gating before enabling low-latency routing; on failure mark as 'warm-only' and notify owner
Risk: overly strict schema prevents interesting experimental models. Mitigation: 'experimental' flag allows ingest with partial hints and funnels to a separate exploratory catalog bucket
Risk: HF repo deref delays. Mitigation: allow 'private' with signed artifact + provenance link as temporary substitute
outcome_metrics: Manual-review rate for community submissions decreases by 40% within first month
Percent of catalog entries with a valid compat-hint payload >= 85% after 30 days
Incidence of runtime regressions attributable to wrong compatibility hints <= prior baseline
